To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have engineered homodimeric proteins that bind to DNA and form DNA loops, and we have used them to control gene expression in bacteria.

we have designed a novel class of transcriptional control proteins that can mimic regulatory properties of natural bacterial transcriptional regulators, and that we have used these proteins to control expression of genes in living bacteria.

1) engineered DNA looping can be used as a new method for transcriptional control in E. coli; 2) DNA looping can be controlled using small molecules; and 3) the DNA looping proteins are based on the dimerization domain of FKBP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the engineering of novel genetic switches in bacteria.
the development of new tools for genetic control of bacterial gene expression.
understanding and applying the principles of DNA looping to engineer synthetic transcription factors for gene control in bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is a very elegant approach to tune gene expression in bacteria and that similar principles might be applicable in eukaryotic cells.
this study demonstrates that DNA looping can be used as a new approach for transcriptional control in living bacteria.
we have engineered a new class of transcription factors that can be used to control gene expression in bacteria by small molecule inducers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel approach to control gene expression using engineered proteins that mimic the DNA looping mechanisms found in natural transcriptional regulators.
we engineered a new class of transcriptional activator proteins that can bind DNA and activate gene expression by looping DNA.

the engineered dimeric DNA looping protein (TALEDs) is a new strategy for gene regulation, which mimics the regulatory characteristics of the classical Escherichiacoli lactose, galacatose and tryptophean operon promoter, including induction or corepression by small molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNA looping can be used for transcriptional control in prokaryotes, using engineered proteins that are not natural transcription factors.
the principles of natural gene regulation can be used for engineering synthetic gene circuits.
DNA looping can provide a simple, modular and robust strategy for engineering transcriptional control of genes.
